title: fix(post): Fanuc-family mill posts state the clearance Z before the first X/Y traverse
body:
## What changed

The second half of #1616 (PR #1632 did grblHAL, TinyG and Carvera; #1618 set the rule and wording on Tormach). `fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `sinumerik.cps` and `heidenhain.cps` no longer write the first move after `G43 H..` (or the TNC tool call) as one combined rapid from wherever the tool change left the tip. At the program's start and after every tool change, the first motion is preceded by:

1. a Z-only rapid to the section's `ClearancePlane`, else its `RetractPlane`, never below the move's own Z;
2. X/Y alone at that height (left out when the first rapid already is at that height - it is then the traverse itself);
3. for a feed, arc or probing move, a rapid down to the stream's start Z when that is lower;

then the move as the stream states it. A canned cycle read as the first motion is positioned over its hole at the stated height first. A stream that states neither plane is refused by name, and **the refused move is not written** - nor any later motion of that section while X/Y stay unknown (the rest of the section is refused cleanly; review of this PR), so no combined `G00 X.. Y.. Z..` from an unknown height reaches the program text. The wording is #1618/#1632's: `first X/Y traverse with no clearance height stated (no ClearancePlane or RetractPlane) - the post will not rapid X/Y at an unknown height` (prefixed `operation <name>: ` where the post knows it).

Each dialect writes its own rapid: `G00 Z..` (Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan), `G0 Z..` (Haas, 840D). The Heidenhain post is the TNC's ISO dialect, so its form is `G00 G40 G90 Z+..*` - the manual's own positioning block (the section's first motion block carries G40 G90), not `L Z.. FMAX`.

The issue's example, `synth_fanuc.nc`: `G00 X20 Y10 Z-3` after `G43 H02` is now `G00 Z5` / `G00 X20 Y10` / `G00 X20 Y10 Z-3`.

### Frame decision: G43.4 / TCP and rotary paths - correct in the frame, not refused

Recorded in `docs/decisions/1633-fanuc-first-traverse-clearance.md`.
- **Fanuc and Doosan, tilted first record (G43.4):** the rapids are written after the record's own `tilt()`, i.e. after `G43.4 H..` is armed. Z is then the tip's Z in the work offset - the frame the stream states its planes and words in. No rotary word rides the inserted blocks; the rotaries turn only on the record itself, at its target, as before.
- **Doosan indexing path (4th axis, no TCP):** the rapids are in G43 (the frame of the record's own words) with the table still clamped; the index (M11, the move, M10) is the record's.
- **Haas, Mazak, 840D, TNC:** they refuse tilted records (`tiltOk`), so the rapids are always upright.
- Dropped: refusing a tilted first record whose pose is unknown (every rapid of a real rotary program states its pose, so every 5-axis program would be refused at its start); writing the Z before the G43.4 arm (G43 is machine-Z length comp, so a tilted tip would not be at the stated height); inserting the Z line alone (the diagonal from clearance to a first target below the stock top would still cross the part).

## How tested

Pinning suite (new): `crates/post/tests/first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family.rs`, #1632's five-test shape over all six posts plus four:
- `the_first_traverse_after_a_tool_change_states_the_clearance_z_first`
- `the_retract_plane_serves_when_no_clearance_plane_is_stated`
- `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` (also asserts no X/Y motion - neither the bare traverse nor the combined rapid - is written after the refusal, for every post)
- `the_traverse_is_never_below_the_moves_own_height`
- `a_feed_first_move_rapids_down_from_the_stated_clearance`
- `a_cycle_first_is_positioned_over_its_hole_at_the_stated_clearance`
- `the_tnc_states_the_height_in_its_positioning_block_form`
- `under_g43_4_the_height_is_stated_after_the_arm_and_before_any_turn` (fanuc, doosan-dnm on the tilthead)
- `on_the_doosan_index_path_the_height_is_stated_with_the_table_clamped`

Also re-pinned: `fanuc_post::rtcp_output_arms_once_and_walks_the_angles` (the `G00 Z5` sits right after `G43.4 H01`), `doosan_dnm_post::doosan_dnm_index_names_only_a_stated_rotary` (`G00 Z10` before `M11`), `heidenhain_cycles::g200_uses_surface_relative_q_values_and_keeps_the_explicit_hop` (`G00 G40 G90 Z-40`, then `G00 X+10 Y+20`).

### Mutations (each restored after)

Per post, run against `first_traverse_clearance_fanuc_family`:

| post | drop the Z line | replace the refusal |
|---|---|---|
| fanuc | 6 red (incl. the G43.4 frame test) | `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` red |
| haas | 5 red | refusal test red |
| mazak | 5 red | refusal test red |
| doosan-dnm | 7 red (incl. G43.4 frame and index-path tests) | refusal test red |
| sinumerik | 5 red | refusal test red |
| heidenhain | 6 red (incl. the TNC block-form test) | refusal test red |

Putting the write back after the refusal (`if (!xyFirst(..)) return;` -> `xyFirst(..);`): `a_first_traverse_with_no_stated_plane_is_refused_by_name` red for each of the six posts.

### Gate

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final tree: post suites ok, app suites ok (all app suites ran: shared test code changed), 14.5 min, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all green. (No `import_step_guard` flake hit.)

### Test fixtures

Hand-written streams that stated no plane now state one, as `post::dump` does for every real section (comp, comp_plane, axis_direction_cli, work_offset_index, heidenhain_cycles, heidenhain_block_form, heidenhain_arc_centre, doosan_dnm_post, fanuc_post, vendor_mch_cli, arc_planes, inverted_support; app: doosan_dnm_a_state, fourth_axis_pose, rotary_feed_cap, program_units, sinumerik_safe_retract, sinumerik_work_offsets). `regression_models` line counts +1 each (the stated height). The test readers `macro_b` (inverted_probe) and `inverted_support::controller_events` (inverted_equivalence) now read a Z-only move before X/Y are known as the stated height, not a move from an unknown position / a CAM motion. `crates/post/tests/recorded/inputs/inverted_probe.cnc` regenerated (one added `PARAM ClearancePlane`).

Carried identical hunks, as #1632 did with #1618: `crates/app/tests/common/legacy_program.rs` (byte-identical to #1618's and #1632's) and `crates/app/tests/post_spindle_rule_all.rs` (byte-identical to #1632's).

## Moved goldens (161)

Every change checked by script (`difflib` over the old and new golden, TNC block numbers, `*`, `+` signs and the TNC's G40 G90 normalized away): no line deleted or replaced, and every inserted block is `G00 Z..` (88) or `G00 Z..` + `G00 X.. Y..` (77), at the first motion after a tool change; every tool change in each file has exactly one such block. No snapshot PNG touched.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/` (25): arc_planes, contour_control_comp, contour_disc_hole, contour_plate_with_hole, contour_tangential_lead, contour_wear_comp, drill_peck, drill_plate, face_square_40x40, face_square_40x40_stepped, pocket_waterline_plate_with_island, pocket_zigzag_plate_with_island, slot_fullwidth_centerline, slot_wide_channel_rows, synth_doosan-dnm, synth_fanuc, synth_haas, synth_heidenhain, synth_mazak, synth_sinumerik, tap_plate, thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form, thread_mill_m8_multi_form, trace_plate_with_hole, trochoid_slot_small

## Not exercised

Taken on trust (also in `docs/decisions/1633-fanuc-first-traverse-clearance.md`):
- **The clearance plane over the tool-change X/Y.** The Z-only rapid at the tool-change X/Y trusts the stated clearance plane (else retract plane) to clear everything under that X/Y - vise, fixture, tool rack, rotary table. The post cannot know what is there. This is safer than main's combined diagonal when the tip stood below the part top (the #1614 case), and **not** safer when something under the tool-change X/Y is taller than the clearance: the vertical descent meets it.
- **G43.4 with an unknown rotary pose (fanuc, doosan-dnm).** The Z / X / Y lines come after the arm, with the rotaries at the previous section's pose (or wherever they stood at program start). No control has run it.
- **The Doosan index path.** Z in G43 with the table clamped at its previous index; whether the clearance clears the part at that index is the plane's promise.
- **End-to-end blocking** on a warning is the callers' job: the app paths refuse to write (`crates/app/src/posting.rs:588`, `posting_mounts.rs:248`, `posting_per_op.rs:168`); the `post` CLI (`crates/post/src/bin/post.rs:163`) writes and prints warnings, by design (its `.refusal` cases). The post now leaves the refused move out regardless.

- No real control run (PathPilot Hub covers Tormach only); the dialect forms come from the posts' own published sources.
- Windows arms of per-OS pinned readings; the UI crate (no UI code touched).

Changelog: Fanuc, Haas, Mazak, Doosan DNM, Sinumerik 840D and Heidenhain posts state the section's clearance Z (ClearancePlane, else RetractPlane) as a Z-only rapid, then X/Y at it, before the first X/Y traverse after each tool change; a stream that states neither plane is refused by name (#1633, #1616)

Effort: high (no escalation). Fork synced at upstream/main db6fd5d4 (worktree from upstream/main).

Fixes #1633
